assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a whole field by showing that band topology yields robust boundary states, a clean and general mechanism that crosses condensed matter, materials and cold atoms. The Kane-Mele Z2 classification and the HgTe quantum spin Hall prediction and observation form a theory-plus-experiment story I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (quantum spin Hall effect in graphene, Z2 invariant). Molenkamp led the experimental observation in HgTe wells. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect, and Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Roy made the 3D case, but these names are not in the supplied credit. This leaves a real fairness question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently across many materials and over fifteen years, including ARPES on Bi-based 3D topological insulators. The interpretation is stable and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and of the 3D topological insulator pioneers, from the supplied credit is a real allocation concern.
I have not independently verified the exact priority chronology from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active-matter hydrodynamics shows that self-propelled particles with an alignment rule can show long-range order in two dimensions, with anomalous fluctuations and universal exponents. This is exactly the kind of simple, universal mechanism in nonequilibrium statistical physics that I value, and it has had large influence on soft matter and biological physics.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal flocking model with the numerical evidence. Toner and Tu gave the hydrodynamic theory and the exponents. Ramaswamy and collaborators founded the hydrodynamics of active fluids and gels. Tu is not in the supplied credit, and Toner's contribution is inseparable from Tu's, so the credit is incomplete. Toner, Ramaswamy and Vicsek is nevertheless a defensible trio.
assessment.maturity: Theory is mature and confirmed in several experimental systems (bacterial suspensions, Janus colloids, vibrated granular layers, cell monolayers). Quantitative tests of the exact exponents are less clean than the qualitative ones, but recognition is timely given how large the field now is.
uncertainties: Tu's role in the Toner-Tu theory is not covered by the supplied credit.
Quantitative experimental tests of the predicted scaling exponents are limited, and I am not certain of their current status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases, from the Aharonov-Bohm effect to Berry's adiabatic phase, underlie much of modern physics (Berry curvature, Chern numbers, polarization, quantum Hall physics, topological matter). It is a foundational idea with an elegant mechanism and a long record of experimental confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Berry's 1984 paper is the clear decisive contribution to the adiabatic phase. Aharonov and Bohm (with Bohm deceased) provided the earlier phase effect, and Aharonov-Anandan generalized the phase. The two-name credit is clean, but Bohm cannot be recognized and Ehrenberg and Siday are historical precedents. Simon's holonomy interpretation is also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in optics, NMR, neutron interferometry, electron holography and solid-state physics for decades. It is not at all premature. The risk is that the recognition could be viewed as overdue or as awkwardly split from the topological-phase prizes already given.
uncertainties: The historical credit chain (Ehrenberg-Siday, Bohm, Pancharatnam, Aharonov-Anandan, Simon) makes any short list partly arbitrary.
The Aharonov-Bohm effect is itself a foundations topic, and the committee's view on whether it counts as a discovery or an interpretive insight is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned Hubbard-type models into controllable laboratory systems (superfluid to Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopes, quantum simulation). This links strongly with my interest in statistical mechanics of interacting many-body systems and the experiment-theory coupling is outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the optical-lattice Hubbard emulation with Jaksch et al., Bloch and Greiner realized and developed the experimental programme (Mott transition 2002, microscopes). The supplied credit lists four names, and I choose three. Greiner's microscope and Mott work are also central, so omitting him is a real cost. Jaksch is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have confirmed the main results and the field is mature, although the quantum-simulation payoff for open problems (e.g. Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram) is still developing. The recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Choosing three of four credited names (Greiner excluded) is contentious.
Overlap with the trapped-ion candidate through Cirac and Zoller complicates a prize configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the experimental realization in ion traps (entanglement, gates, algorithms) is a keystone of quantum information science. The idea is clear and has had a lasting effect on quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive 1995 theoretical proposal. Experimental credit is distributed among Blatt, Wineland (already a laureate in 2012), Monroe, and others. Blatt is a reasonable experimental representative, but the allocation is arguable and Wineland's earlier prize partly overlaps in subject matter.
assessment.maturity: Experimental realization is robust and replicated in several groups, and trapped-ion platforms are now commercial. Timely, but the 2012 prize and the 2025 prize on circuit-based quantum devices reduce the novelty for a committee.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland) and the 2025 prize may lower the priority.
Experimental credit allocation is unresolved (Monroe and others outside the supplied credit).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems are exact results for nonequilibrium systems that generalize the second law and the Green-Kubo and Onsager relations far from equilibrium. They are universal, rigorously derived and fit well with my own area of stochastic processes, and they underpin single-molecule thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: The attribution is the weakest part. Evans, Cohen and Morriss, Gallavotti and Cohen, Jarzynski, Crooks, Kurchan, Lebowitz and Spohn, Seifert, and Bochkov and Kuzovlev all made key contributions. Any three-person list is open to challenge, and the named trio omits Crooks in particular.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in colloids, RNA pulling, and electronic systems, and well understood theoretically. It is mature, but its impact on physics outside stochastic thermodynamics is moderate, so the committee may judge it as less than Nobel scale.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among many contributors is badly unresolved.
It is unclear whether the practical or conceptual impact is broad enough for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical discovery that identical particles in two dimensions can have fractional statistics (anyons) is a conceptually beautiful result with deep implications for the fractional quantum Hall effect and topological quantum computation.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim's 1977 paper and Wilczek's 1982 work are the decisive theoretical sources, and all three are on the supplied credit. Halperin and Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek applied the idea to the quantum Hall states and are not credited. The three-person set is fair for the pure theory.
assessment.maturity: Experimental evidence for anyonic braiding statistics emerged in 2020 (quantum Hall interferometers and collision experiments in graphene and GaAs), but these are recent and still few in number, and non-Abelian anyons are unconfirmed. Recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation is recent and from few groups, and I cannot judge how settled it is.
Whether Halperin and Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek should share credit is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle in cells (P granules, nucleoli, condensates) is a broad shift in cell biology that draws on soft-matter physics. The statistical-physics framing is attractive to me, although the work is closer to biology than physics.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne, Hyman and Jülicher demonstrated liquid-like P granules and provided the physical theory. Rosen, Parker, Pappu and others had parallel roles, and the biological/chemistry credit may belong in a different prize category.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and fast moving, and it is under debate how widely phase separation is functionally relevant in vivo versus an in vitro artifact. Recognition may be premature for a physics prize.
uncertainties: Functional relevance of condensates in living cells is still contested.
Whether the committee regards this as physics or as biology or chemistry.
